_method_note: MEMBERSHIP IS BY CLOSURE MINUS CUTS, not by name. A function is in this ledger because the root reaches it without passing through a declared wall, and it is neither a shared helper nor already owned by another domain. Measured for this run: 741 reachable raw, 0 cut walls (presentation/sound/net -- reached but never descended through), 42 shared helpers held as frontier, {'ai': 162} owned elsewhere. THE FAILURE MODE IS THE INVERSE OF THE NAME-PREFIX ONE: nothing drops out when a function is renamed, but a WRONGLY PLACED WALL silently removes an entire subtree, and a subtree that never appears is invisible. Re-read select.cut_prefixes in the profile before concluding that something is absent, and prefer widening a wall to adding a hand override. Layering is computed on member-only edges, because only members are ever armed and only they can nest.

No offline oracle written this slice -- VERIFICATION DEBT for a future -V companion item, matching the SIM1D-V/SIM1E-V precedent. SIXTH SLICE (2026-08-21, session 2026-08-21-1744): re-read tmp/decomp_sim/llm_strat_unit_state_enter_storage_begin_0047ff50.asm in full to write an offline oracle (arm_ready:false -- broad closure via llm_strat_storage_board_unit) and found a REAL PRESERVE-BUG REGRESSION: the .asm's abort call (LAB_00480018, unit_set_state(STOP_TO_DEFAULT)) has NO return/branch-out -- it falls straight through into the SAME storage_can_enter/door logic the ready==true path uses (LAB_00480012's JZ 0x00480022 and LAB_00480018's fallthrough both land at 0x00480022), independently corroborated by the Ghidra .c draft, which also has no `return` there. The existing .cpp had an early `return` after the abort call -- a Law-2 violation (a corrected bug, not a preserved one) rather than a translation of a genuinely different original. FIXED in sim_unit_state_enter.cpp (removed the `return`, added a PRESERVE-BUG note at the fix site and in the .h SHAPE banner). Net effect: on the not-ready arm, storage_can_enter still runs; if it grants entry the door still gets claimed and board_unit still fires (the STOP_TO_DEFAULT set moments earlier stands, since nothing overwrites it); if denied, door_waiter_count still increments and unit_set_state(ENTER_WAIT) OVERWRITES the earlier STOP_TO_DEFAULT (both are the same global last-write-wins state field) -- so STOP_TO_DEFAULT on this arm is transient and only externally observable via can_enter granting on the SAME tick. Wrote and mutation-tested sim_unit_state_enter_storage_begin_selftest.cpp (6 cases: the two independent not-ready gates in isolation via can_enter=1, the ready+claim path with the door mutex/board_unit call, the ready+wait path with the door_waiter_count/ENTER_WAIT transition, and case 3b making the PRESERVE-BUG itself explicit -- not-ready AND can_enter==0, asserting the double unit_set_state call and the still-incrementing door_waiter_count). Mutation-tested by RE-INTRODUCING the removed `return` and confirming 4 checks failed by name across cases 1 and 3b (exactly the ones that depend on fallthrough), reverted, reconfirmed clean. Full mh.sln build (mh.dll + net_selftest.exe) clean both before and after the revert. net_selftest simtest 5639/0 -> 5656/0 (+17, the 6th check row it prints being case 3b's non-canonical 3-assertion shape plus 14 from cases 1-5). VERIFIED/T2 (armable in principle -- the closure is broad because of storage_board_unit's own downstream reach, not because THIS function's own writes are unbounded; a real T1 remains available if a future rig scenario reaches it).
